summary: Created an opsbot account on node1 (RHEL 7) with an ed25519 keypair, authorized that public key for opsbot on node2 (RHEL 7), and enforced key-only SSH authentication for opsbot on both nodes via a Match User opsbot sshd_config block (PasswordAuthentication no, AuthenticationMethods publickey). Implemented entirely with Ansible, run from node3 (the only node with ansible/ansible-playbook installed, used strictly as the control node). Since ansible-core 2.20 on node3 requires Python 3 on managed nodes but node1/node2 only have Python 2.7 with no working package repos, all target tasks use Ansible's raw module (no target-side Python dependency) instead of standard modules. Verified opsbot can SSH from node1 to node2 non-interactively with the key, and that password-preferred SSH attempts against opsbot on both nodes are rejected (Permission denied (publickey)) while sshd reports AuthenticationMethods=publickey for that user. Completed the mandatory restart protocol: captured boot_id/uptime/service baselines on all three nodes, rebooted node1, node2, and node3 one at a time (never concurrently), confirmed each node's boot_id changed and command execution resumed, and re-verified opsbot's account, keys, sshd policy, and live node1-to-node2 SSH access after each reboot, culminating in a full successful re-run of the Ansible playbook after node3's own reboot.
actions_performed: Surveyed node1 (RHEL7), node2 (RHEL7), node3 (Ubuntu 24.04 with ansible-core 2.20) to identify node3 as the sole viable Ansible control node
Authorized CLUSTER_SSH_PUBKEY on the antrieb user's authorized_keys on node1 and node2 so node3 could reach them via SSH with passwordless sudo
Installed CLUSTER_SSH_PRIVKEY on node3 and built an Ansible inventory (inventory.ini) targeting node1/node2 as user antrieb with become=sudo

Discovered ansible-core 2.20 requires Python 3 on managed nodes (ping module failed); node1/node2 only have Python 2.7 and no enabled/working yum repos (subscription-manager disabled, EPEL install timed out), so switched all target tasks to Ansible's raw module which needs no remote Python

Wrote /root/ansible/opsbot.yml: play 1 creates opsbot + ed25519 keypair on node1 and adds a key-only Match User opsbot sshd block; play 2 creates opsbot on node2, authorizes node1's public key, and adds the same sshd Match block; play 3 verifies non-interactive opsbot SSH from node1 to node2
Fixed StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new incompatibility with node1's old OpenSSH client by using StrictHostKeyChecking=no
Ran the playbook successfully end-to-end and re-ran it to confirm idempotency

Verified via sshd -T -C user=opsbot that AuthenticationMethods=publickey and PasswordAuthentication=[REDACTED] apply to opsbot on both nodes, and confirmed a live SSH attempt with PreferredAuthentications=password is rejected with Permission denied (publickey) on both nodes
Captured boot_id/uptime/service baselines on node1, node2, node3
Rebooted node1 via backgrounded 'sudo systemctl reboot', polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed and opsbot/sshd/keys/policy intact
Rebooted node2 the same way, confirmed boot_id changed, opsbot/authorized_keys/sshd policy intact, and re-verified live node1-to-node2 opsbot SSH still works
Rebooted node3 (control node) the same way, confirmed boot_id changed, and re-ran the full Ansible playbook successfully post-reboot as final end-to-end proof

evidence.requirement: opsbot account created on node1 with SSH keypair
evidence.summary: Ansible playbook run shows opsbot user creation and keygen tasks as ok; sudo ls/cat on node1 shows opsbot-owned .ssh dir (700) with id_ed25519/id_ed25519.pub

evidence.requirement: opsbot on node1 has key-based SSH access to run commands as opsbot on node2
evidence.summary: Direct SSH from node1 as opsbot to node2 as opsbot using PreferredAuthentications=publickey succeeds (returns whoami=opsbot, hostname=node2); reproduced inside the Ansible playbook's verification task; re-confirmed after node2's reboot

evidence.requirement: node2 authorized_keys contains node1's opsbot public key with correct ownership/permissions
evidence.summary: sudo cat/ls on node2 shows authorized_keys (600, opsbot:opsbot) containing exactly node1's opsbot public key; identical content confirmed again after node2's reboot

evidence.requirement: Key-based authentication required for opsbot on node1 (password auth blocked)
evidence.summary: sshd -T -C user=opsbot on node1 reports PasswordAuthentication=[REDACTED] and AuthenticationMethods=publickey; live SSH attempt with PreferredAuthentications=password returns 'Permission denied (publickey)'; same policy confirmed again after node1's reboot

evidence.requirement: Key-based authentication required for opsbot on node2 (password auth blocked)
evidence.summary: sshd -T -C user=opsbot on node2 reports PasswordAuthentication=[REDACTED] and AuthenticationMethods=publickey; live SSH attempt with PreferredAuthentications=password returns 'Permission denied (publickey)'; same policy confirmed again after node2's reboot

evidence.requirement: Implementation performed via Ansible from the correct control node
